Speculative cost concern: a scalar subquery only loses the guard if it sits under a null-propagating node with the checked operand (uncommon), and SQL engines don't guarantee CASE short-circuits subquery evaluation anyway; no concrete regression shown.

SqlBinaryExpression.GetHashCode is recursive, so hashing every subtree is O(n*depth), but n is a projection expression and this runs once per compiled query behind the shape gate, as the cluster itself concedes; not actionable.

DropNotNullChecks only removes whole conjuncts and returns the surviving side directly (left is null ? right : ...); every surviving conjunct was already visited and simplified before this point and no constant is ever introduced, so nothing is left trivially true/false to re-simplify.
